newsitem.title: USA: American General gains clout with deal.
newsitem.headline: American General gains clout with deal.

text.p: American General Corp's proposed $1.8 billion acquisition of USLIFE Corp bolsters its position in the upper-income life insurance market and establishes it as one of the nation's largest life insurers.
The deal also gives American General additional opportunities to sell life insurance products through banks with the acquisition of USLIFE's credit insurance operation, analysts said.
It also firmly establishes American General as one of the industry's major consolidators, they said.
The $1.8 billion stock deal, which was announced earlier today, is expected to close in the second quarter of 1997 and is expected to contribute to earnings in 1998.
"All of a sudden, American General is a very large, broad-based, multi-faceted operation that's one of the major life players right now," Dean Witter analyst Michael Lewis said.
And the company is "continuing to position itself to compete in a much more competitive environment where the barriers are down between financial sectors."
Lewis said he upgraded his opinion on American General to buy from neutral following the announcement of the deal.

American General catapults into fifth place in the U.S. life insurance industry on the basis of total admitted assets from 11th place without the acquisition, said A.M. Best vice president Michael Albanese.
USLIFE ranked 58th on the basis of total admitted assets, he said.

American General already had a strong position in the so-called home service business, with its American General Life and Accident Insurance Co, which provides more affordable life insurance to lower-income customers, Albanese said.
American General's place in the middle-income market was strengthened with the acquisition of Franklin Life Insurance Co in 1995.

Now USLIFE will provide added size and scope to American General's American General Life Insurance Co, which markets life insurance to middle- and upper-income customers through general agents, analysts said.
"It really enhances their position in the general agency market," Conning & Co analyst Jeffrey Schuman said.

"That business is the smallest of their life insurance operations and was probably most in need of adding some additional back office and distribution scale and USLIFE should fit that need pretty nicely," Schuman said.
"It gives them more scale in the part of the life insurance operation that needed it the most."
He also expects American General taking advantage of USLIFE's credit insurance operation to expand the sale of life insurance through banks.
American General already has a credit insurance operation and also has a 46 percent stake in Western National, which sells annuities through banks.

But USLIFE, which recently began selling life insurance through its credit insurance business, will give American General increased opportunities to sell its life insurance through banks, Schuman said.
"We would expect that American General will capitalize on that initiative and move more aggressively there," Schuman said.
